sections.html:
The Brown County Register of Deeds is in the Northern Building, Room 260, at 305 E. Walnut Street in Green Bay. Mail goes to P.O. Box 23600, Green Bay, WI 54305-3600. The phone number is 920-448-4470.

Public hours run 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 7:30 to 11:30 a.m. on Friday. Walk-in real estate recordings stop earlier, at 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 10:30 a.m. on Friday. If your closing falls late in the day or on a Friday, aim for the earlier cutoff and call ahead to confirm hours.

One office records the deeds, land contracts, mortgages and plats for the whole county, and it also issues vital records. Each recorded document is stamped with the date, hour and minute (s. 59.43) and filed in the order it arrived. A deed is recorded here no matter which city, village or town the house sits in.

sections.h2: Tag-less recording and the Swift Agreement
sections.html:
Brown County records without a paper tag. Anyone who sends paper documents for recording must include a completed Swift Agreement, which sets up access to the official copy once the document is recorded.

After recording, you get an email with a secure link. The link allows up to three printed copies and works for seven days, so download the PDF the day it arrives. A seller who wants a permanent copy for the closing binder should save it right then.

State law adds a delivery rule. A register must send recorded documents to the recipient the submitter names once adequate postage is provided, unless the submitter agrees to another arrangement (s. 59.43(1c)(g)). Put the recipient and an email address on the Swift Agreement so the link reaches the right person.

The county's land records search system is called Laredo, and it is available by advance appointment only. Call 920-448-4470 to book a time. Do not count on a same-day walk-in search the morning of a closing.

Copies of recorded documents cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page, plus $1 to certify. The state sets those prices (s. 59.43(2)(b)). Most sellers never need to search at all, because the title company runs the search for the sale. Give it the parcel number from your tax bill and ask whether it will pull what it needs.

Recording a deed, mortgage or similar document costs $30, the flat rate in s. 59.43(2)(ag). Payment is due in advance.

Document or serviceFee
Deed, mortgage, satisfaction or land contract$30
Cemetery, subdivision or condominium plat$50
Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added page
Certification of a copy$1 more
State transfer fee (if the sale is not exempt)Paid by the seller, on top of the recording fee

The register collects the transfer fee when it takes the deed, so plan to pay both amounts at the same counter visit or in the same e-recording batch.

sections.h2: Transfer fee on a home sale
sections.html:
The seller pays $3 for every $1,000 of value, which is 30 cents per $100 or fraction of $100 (s. 77.22). Use the sale price, and count any mortgage balance the buyer takes over as part of it. For a gift or other transfer with no price, an unappraised property is reported at the estimated full value shown on the latest property tax bill. Appliances, furniture and other personal property go on a separate line and stay out of the fee base.

A few points matter in Brown County deals:

  • Parts of Howard and Wrightstown lie in Outagamie County. A transfer with parcels in two counties needs a separate return for each county.
  • A deed that finishes a land contract owes no second fee if the right fee was paid when the contract was recorded (s. 77.25(17)).
  • No city, village, town or county may charge its own fee on a conveyance that the state exempts (s. 77.256).
  • Every grantor and grantee on the deed gets listed on the return individually.

Each month the register passes the fees and returns to the county treasurer by the 15th, and the county keeps 20 percent (ss. 77.23 and 77.24). Gifts between parent and child, transfers by will and foreclosure deeds to the mortgage holder are among the exemptions in s. 77.25.

A deed is turned away when it misses a format item in s. 59.43(2m) or carries a Social Security number. The register may also refuse a whole set of related documents if one of them fails. Check these points before anyone signs:

  • A blank 3 by 3 inch space in the upper right corner of page one.
  • The parcel identification number for each parcel affected.
  • Return information on the first page, unless the document is recorded electronically.
  • White paper, at least 20 pound, 8.5 inches wide and 11 or 14 inches long, with no hinged pages.
  • Legible black, blue or red ink and clearly printed grantor, grantee and notary names.
  • No Social Security number anywhere in the document.

The register does not judge value or exemptions, so those entries are the filer's responsibility. Knowingly falsifying a value on a transfer return can bring a fine of up to $1,000, up to a year in the county jail, or both.

sections.h2: Recording step by step for a seller
sections.html:
Most Brown County sales follow the same path, and the title company usually handles it. If you are handling the paperwork yourself, work through it in this order.

  1. Get the parcel number from your tax bill and put it on the deed.
  2. Check the deed against the format list above, including the blank corner and return address.
  3. Complete the transfer return with the sale price and any exemption.
  4. Fill out the Swift Agreement if you are sending paper, and name the person who should receive the recorded copy.
  5. Deliver everything before the walk-in cutoff, with the $30 recording fee and the transfer fee.
  6. Download the emailed copy within seven days.

Selling for cash does not skip any of this. The deed is still recorded and the transfer fee still applies. What a cash sale cuts out is the buyer's loan approval, so fewer lender documents are in the stack and the closing date depends mostly on how soon the deed is ready.

Brown County is the fourth most populous county in Wisconsin and part of the Green Bay metro area. Population is 275,803, up 2.6 percent since 2020, and there are 118,788 housing units. About 66.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $266,000. Median gross rent is $1,031. Green Bay and De Pere are the two cities, with villages including Allouez, Ashwaubenon, Bellevue, Howard, Suamico and Pulaski around them.

Property tax is a separate matter from recording. The county treasurer collects first-installment taxes for only some Brown County municipalities, so check your bill for the right payee.

faqs.q: What are the Brown County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Public hours are 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 7:30 to 11:30 a.m. Friday. Walk-in real estate recordings are taken until 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 10:30 a.m. Friday. Call 920-448-4470 to confirm before you go.

faqs.q: Do I need a Swift Agreement to record a deed in Brown County?
faqs.a: Yes, if you submit paper documents. The county records without a tag, and paper filers must include a completed Swift Agreement. The official copy then arrives by emailed link that allows up to three printed copies within seven days.

faqs.q: How do I search Brown County land records?
faqs.a: The search system is called Laredo and is open by advance appointment only. Call 920-448-4470 to schedule, or ask your title company to run the search. Copies cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page.

faqs.q: How much is the real estate transfer fee in Brown County?
faqs.a: It is the same statewide: 30 cents per $100 of value, paid by the seller under s. 77.22. Gifts between parent and child, transfers by will and foreclosure deeds to the mortgage holder are among the exemptions in s. 77.25.

faqs.q: Can the Brown County register record a deed that has a Social Security number?
faqs.a: No. Section 59.43(1m) bars a register of deeds from recording a document that contains an individual's Social Security number. Remove it before you submit the deed.
